exercise.name: Cable Zercher Squat

reference.title: Cable Zercher Squat (male)
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (straight cable bar from a low pulley held in the elbow crooks, squat).

exercise.mechanics: Compound (squat with a front-loaded Zercher hold)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace before you lower; breathe out through the sticking point on the way up.

prescription.load: User-chosen cable weight; the elbows and upper back limit the load before the legs do
prescription.progression: More reps, then more weight; a pad on the bar if the elbow crooks get sore

cues.text: Cradle the cable bar in the crooks of the elbows, hands clasped in front of the chest; step back from the low pulley, feet about shoulder width, toes out.
Sit down between the heels, chest tall, elbows forward; knees track over the toes.
Thighs at or a little below parallel; elbows just inside the knees; back flat.
Drive up through the whole foot, keeping the chest up and the bar tight to the body.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the upper back as the bar pulls forward
mistakes.fix: Chest proud, elbows up a little; lighter weight.
Sit back between the heels; weight over the mid-foot.
Push the knees out over the toes.
Keep the elbows bent hard and the hands clasped high.

kinematics.norm: About shoulder width, toes out about 15-20 degrees (common coaching; Zawadka 2020 used shoulder width)
About 100-120 degrees with the thighs at parallel or a bit below (clinical opinion); depth is driven mostly by knee range (Zawadka 2020)
Not specified by the sources for this depth
More upright than a back squat because the load is in front (clinical opinion); more lean moves demand from knee to hip (Straub 2024)
Bar in the elbow crooks, elbows bent, hands clasped in front of the chest (common coaching; clinical opinion)
About 2 s down, about 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #21628, Cable Zercher Squat (male), video (movement reference)
Zawadka et al. 2020, How are squat timing and kinematics in the sagittal plane related to squat depth? (J Sports Sci Med 19:500-507)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)
Gullett, Tillman, Gutierrez & Chow 2009, a biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals (J Strength Cond Res 23(1):284-292; PubMed 19002072)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
The bar presses into the elbow crooks: use a pad or a towel, and stop if the elbows hurt.
Knee pain: squat to a comfortable depth.
Low-back pain: keep the chest up; a front load that drags you forward means the weight is too heavy.
Step back from the pulley carefully and return the bar under control.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main knee extensors through the squat (clinical opinion); front-loaded squats keep the trunk more upright with similar leg demand (Gullett 2009, front squat).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Main knee extensors through the squat (clinical opinion); front-loaded squats keep the trunk more upright with similar leg demand (Gullett 2009, front squat).

muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hips out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hips from the deep, wide position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hips from the deep, wide position (clinical opinion).

muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and steady the knee (clinical opinion).

muscleNotes.biceps_l: Hold the elbows bent around the bar (clinical opinion).
